Model, loop, tool layer, permission syst: A coding agent has eight parts: a model, a loop, a tool layer, a permission system, a context budget, instruction files, hooks, and a log. The model is one of the eight. The other seven are the harness, and you can test them.

Falsified by any out-of-scope call that: Any out-of-scope call that succeeds, any write that follows a resource-borne instruction, or a pass obtained by disabling a check falsifies it.
An OAuth resource server since 2025-06-1: The server is an OAuth resource server since 2025-06-18. Clients MUST send an RFC 8707 resource indicator, so a token cannot be replayed at another server. Client ID Metadata Documents recommended since 2025-11-25; Dynamic Client Registration deprecated in 2026-07-28.
Scopes per tool class: read, write, admi: Declare a scope per tool class: read, write, admin. A token without the write scope gets 403 insufficient_scope before the function runs, and the server logs the refusal. In 2026-07-28, tools/list no longer varies per connection, so enforcement lives on tools/call.
2026-07-28 revision; each step names the: 2026-07-28 revision; each step lists the check that stops one attack
No token: 401; WWW-Authenticate names re: No token: 401; WWW-Authenticate carries resource_metadata and scope="notes:read". Client reads RFC 9728 metadata, then AS metadata.
PKCE pair; resource=<canonical server UR: Client makes a PKCE pair, sends resource=<canonical server URI> and the challenged scope, and records the expected issuer. User consents.
Code + iss returned. Client MUST check i: The redirect returns code + iss. Client MUST check iss against the recorded issuer (RFC 9207), then sends code_verifier + resource.
Bearer token on every request. Server ch: The client sends a bearer token on every request. The server checks signature, expiry, audience, and scope per tool. Too little scope: 403 insufficient_scope, scope="notes:write".
Steps 1 to 4 are the client's discipline: Steps 1 to 4 are the client's discipline. Step 5 is yours: the server checks audience and scope on every call and logs each refusal.

Agent Card: identity, skills, endpoints,: An Agent Card carries identity, skills, endpoints, and auth (signed in v1.0). The client sends a Task; the remote agent works it through states (submitted, working, input-required, completed …) and returns Artifacts. Opaque: you do not see its tools or reasoning. 150+ organizations by Apr 2026.
MCP for an observation you can log and v: Use MCP for an observation you can log and validate. Use A2A when the work is somebody else's and you will verify it.
A signed Agent Card proves who is speaki: A signed Agent Card proves which agent is speaking. It proves nothing about whether that agent's artifact is true; your host has to check that.
A folder with a SKILL.md: description al: A skill is a folder with a SKILL.md. The harness always loads the description and loads the body when the skill is invoked or matched. The map stays in context, the procedure on disk. Move multi-step procedures into skills.
Map, not encyclopedia: where the truth l: Map, not encyclopedia: the file says where the truth lives and what must hold, and omits what the agent can derive from code.
OpenAI's claim. Engineers build the envi: OpenAI's report. Engineers build the environment, not the code: a short AGENTS.md, docs as system of record, linters and structural tests. 'Too much guidance becomes non-guidance.'
Role or scope read from the body, a head: The server reads role or scope from the body, a header, or a tool argument. The adversary sends a different value.
Write tool off tools/list, and tools/cal: The write tool is left off tools/list, and tools/call does not check. Under 2026-07-28 lists do not vary per connection.
A defense that exists only as a sentence: A defense that exists only as a sentence, or only while the test runs, leaves the write tool open to the adversary.

Pin the package version and hash, not on: Pin the package version and hash, not only the descriptions. Read the source or provenance before install. Prefer servers from the vendor whose API they call. Each step slows upgrades.
Pinning catches a server that lies to th: Pinning catches a server that changes what it tells the model. It does not check what the server's code does.
